text.p: These are the leading stories in Zimbabwe's Herald newspaper on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Harare City Council now expects the green light to build Kunzwi Dam for its residents, with the government set to pay 20 percent of the total construction cost of Z$2 billion.

- Most of the accidents which occured on Zimbabwean roads during the just ended Easter holidays were caused by excessive drinking, excitement, speeding and lack of courtesy among drivers, police said on Tuesday.

- Two of the three unsuccessful tenderers for Zimbabwe's second cellular phone network licence, Tritel and Supanet, will on Wednesday submit their separate complaints against the awarding of the tender to Telecel.

- Casyman Mining Ltd has sacked a consultant geologist for keeping separate files for black and white employees while a white student who was doing holiday work at the company's Turk Mine has skipped the country following press reports that foreigners at the mine were working without proper permits.
